statement: For a finite straight-edge graph with nonzero edge displacements, edge-midpoint functions satisfying sum_{e incident to v}(p_e-v)F(p_e)=0 at every vertex form a complex vector space of dimension |E|-|V|+c, where c is the number of connected components. In a connected plane graph this equals the number of bounded faces.
assumptions: Distinct edge midpoints (as on the honeycomb lattice); all vertex equations imposed, no nonzero prescribed external flux. Parallel edges can instead be treated as separate edge variables.
source: owner-own-work; local-relation background verified in arXiv:1007.0575v2, Lemma 1, equation (1)
proof_or_counterexample: Orient each edge e=(u,v); put d_e=v-u and J_e=(d_e/2)F(p_e). At u its contribution is J_e, and at v it is -J_e. Thus the equations are BJ=0 for the incidence matrix. Scaling by d_e/2 is invertible. The incidence matrix has rank |V|-c: each component has one row dependency and a spanning-tree minor of rank |V_i|-1. Nullity is |E|-|V|+c. Euler's plane-graph formula gives the face count for a connected embedding.

statement: Let V be a finite honeycomb vertex set, E the edges with both endpoints in V, H the boundary mid-edges with exactly one endpoint in V, and c the number of components of (V,E). Prescribe complex g on H and b_v=sum_{h in H incident to v}(h-v)g(h). Arbitrary complex interior midpoint values F satisfying sum_{p adjacent to v}(p-v)F(p)=0 exist iff sum_{v in C}b_v=0 on every component C. If solvable, their complex affine dimension is |E|-|V|+c. For a connected plane graph this equals the number of bounded faces. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.
assumptions: All hypotheses are included in the statement; arbitrary complex midpoint fields, not the actual SAW path sum.
source: owner-own-work; ATTEMPT.md; local equation from arXiv:1007.0575v2
proof_or_counterexample: Orient internal edges e=(u,v), put d_e=v-u and J_e=d_e F(p_e)/2. The vertex equations become B J=-b, where B has +1 at the tail and -1 at the head and b is the prescribed boundary contribution. Each component has one row dependency. A spanning-tree incidence minor with a root row removed has determinant +/-1 by leaf elimination, so rank B=|V|-c. Its image consists precisely of vectors with zero sum on each component. This proves the compatibility condition and affine dimension |E|-|V|+c. Euler gives the bounded-face count in the connected plane case.

statement: On a honeycomb mesh of side length delta, choose a complete interior hexagonal face with counterclockwise vertices v_0,...,v_5. The complex midpoint field H((v_j+v_{j+1})/2)=delta/(v_{j+1}-v_j), with indices modulo 6 and H=0 elsewhere, satisfies every vertex relation sum_p(p-v)H(p)=0, has six support points of modulus 1, and vanishes at every boundary midpoint. Adding H to a solution preserves every boundary value. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.
assumptions: All hypotheses are included in the statement; arbitrary complex midpoint fields, not the actual SAW path sum.
source: owner-own-work; ATTEMPT.md; local equation from arXiv:1007.0575v2
proof_or_counterexample: On a complete interior hexagon v_0,...,v_5, define H at side midpoints by delta/(v_{j+1}-v_j) and zero at all other midpoints. At v_j the outgoing contribution is delta/2 and the incoming contribution is -delta/2; the third is zero. Other vertices see zero. Since side lengths are delta, the six nonzero values have modulus one. Every prescribed boundary value is unchanged by adding H.

statement: There exist simply connected honeycomb patches tending to a fixed hexagonal domain, with mesh delta_n tending to zero, and arbitrary complex midpoint fields F_n with full boundary trace identically 1, sup norm at most 2, and sum_{p adjacent to v}(p-v)F_n(p)=0 at every vertex, but no subsequence converges locally uniformly to a continuous function near a fixed interior point. One may take F_n=1+H_delta_n on a central face; two midpoints at distance sqrt(3)delta_n/2 have value difference of modulus 1. These fields are not asserted to be SAW observables. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.
assumptions: All hypotheses are included in the statement; arbitrary complex midpoint fields, not the actual SAW path sum.
source: owner-own-work; ATTEMPT.md; local equation from arXiv:1007.0575v2
proof_or_counterexample: The constant field 1 satisfies the vertex identity because the three displacement vectors sum to zero. Add the six-edge field H from the preceding lemma. Then F=1+H has full boundary trace 1 and sup norm at most 2. A face-side midpoint p and the midpoint q of the third edge at the same vertex have separation sqrt(3)delta/2 and value difference of modulus 1. Center the chosen face near a fixed interior point while delta tends to zero. Locally uniform convergence to any continuous f would make the difference at p,q tend to zero, a contradiction. This argument uses arbitrary complex fields; it does not say the actual SAW observable has these modes.

statement: For a connected finite plane honeycomb graph with f bounded faces and compatible prescribed boundary midpoint values, the homogeneous vertex-relation kernel has complex dimension f. Fewer than f additional complex linear conditions cannot determine interior midpoint values uniquely. Exactly f suffice: orient each internal edge, put J_e=(v-u)F(p_e)/2, and impose c_i^T J=0 on the real signed cycle vectors of the bounded faces. These constraints give a unique solution to the algebraic boundary problem; they are not claimed to hold for the actual SAW observable or to prove a scaling limit. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.
assumptions: All hypotheses are included in the statement; arbitrary complex midpoint fields, not the actual SAW path sum.
source: owner-own-work; ATTEMPT.md; local equation from arXiv:1007.0575v2
proof_or_counterexample: The oriented boundaries of the f bounded faces give real cycle vectors c_i. They are independent: zero edge coefficients force neighboring face coefficients to agree, and exterior coefficient zero propagates through the connected dual. Their number f=|E|-|V|+1 equals dim ker B, so C=[c_i] spans the homogeneous kernel. If J=C a and C^T J=0 then C^T C a=0; positive definiteness gives a=0, including complex a. For an inhomogeneous solution J_0, use a=-(C^T C)^(-1)C^T J_0 to satisfy the extra conditions. Fewer than f linear constraints leave a nonzero kernel by rank-nullity. These are algebraic constraints, not conditions proved for the SAW path sum.
